terra.problem: The explanation is flat and procedural, especially the repeated instructions to leave the text as it is. It doesn't sound like Papa Dorin.
The passage doesn't say Hadad was already gone when Joab struck down the males, or that Hadad came back. It says he fled to Egypt.
The text doesn't say Joab never caught Hadad or that Hadad got out before Joab's action.
Pharaoh gave Hadad land; the text doesn't call it a field.
Saying Pharaoh was not recruiting Hadad asserts a motive the text doesn't give.
The text says Hadad asked to return, not that he was sent home. It also doesn't say the request came years later.
The passage says Genubath lived among Pharaoh's sons, but doesn't say he grew up with them.
Calling Rezon a runaway servant rather than a rival king overlooks that the passage also says he ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer, ending with a generic assertion rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
Jeroboam was Solomon's servant, but the passage doesn't say he belonged to Solomon's household.
The text puts Jeroboam over the labor force of the house of Joseph; it doesn't say he was in charge of the workers on the wall.
Ahijah tells Jeroboam to take ten pieces; the text doesn't say he hands the pieces to him.
The passage doesn't say the cloak was never laid down or that none of its pieces ended up on the ground.
The passage connects ten pieces with ten tribes; it doesn't say that each of the twelve pieces represents a tribe.
The closing line is a procedural instruction about keeping to the text, leaving the explanation generic rather than fatherly or conversational.
The passage records Ahijah's words but doesn't say Jeroboam was only listening or that he asked for nothing during the encounter.
This treats the Pharaoh who received Hadad and Shishak, the king who received Jeroboam, as the same person. The passage doesn't identify them as the same king.
This is a flat, repetitive restatement of the verse and answer, with no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The LORD says He will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand. That does not state that Solomon keeps the whole kingdom throughout his lifetime.
The explanation connects the end of the humbling to David's lamp in Jerusalem, but the passage doesn't state that connection.
The passage doesn't say how long Jeroboam stayed in Egypt, so 'a good while' adds a duration.
The passage says Jeroboam remained in Egypt, but doesn't say he stayed hidden or 'tucked away.'
Hadad's being an adversary doesn't establish that he never takes Jerusalem's throne. The passage says Rehoboam succeeds Solomon, not what Hadad never does.
